title: Backpropagation Through a Multilayer Perceptron
summary: How a multilayer perceptron computes gradients: layers that cache on the way forward, vector-Jacobian products instead of Jacobians on the way back, a fused softmax cross-entropy, and numerical gradient checks that prove it's right.
takeaways: Backprop is the chain rule applied layer by layer in reverse, with each layer using only its cache and dout.
Never build Jacobians. For a linear layer, dx = dout·Wᵀ, dW = xᵀ·dout and db = Σ dout over the batch.
A gradient always has the shape of what it differentiates. Shape mismatches reveal missing transposes and unsummed biases.
Fused softmax cross-entropy has gradient (p − onehot)/N. Verify every gradient with central differences.

flow.title: One training step of a 2-layer MLP

steps.label: Forward
steps.detail: x → Linear → ReLU → Linear → logits, caching each layer's inputs.

steps.label: Loss
steps.detail: Stable log-softmax and mean negative log-likelihood of the true class.

steps.label: Backward
steps.detail: Each layer turns dout into dx plus dW and db, in reverse order.

steps.label: Check
steps.detail: Compare against central differences on a tiny network.

steps.label: Update
steps.detail: SGD: every parameter p -= lr · grad.

terms.definition: Stacked fully connected layers with non-linearities between them.
The matrix of all partial derivatives ∂yᵢ/∂xⱼ of a vector function.
Jᵀ·dout, computed directly from the layer's formula without ever forming J.
Values saved during the forward pass that the backward pass needs, such as a layer's input.
Comparing analytic gradients with finite differences, (f(θ+h) − f(θ−h)) / 2h.
Weights drawn with standard deviation √(2/fan_in), which keeps ReLU activations from shrinking or exploding.
